exponential.title: What is an Exponential Function?
exponential.intro: An exponential function is a function where the variable appears in the exponent, creating incredibly rapid growth or decay.
exponential.discovery: Imagine a single bacterium that doubles every hour. After 24 hours, how many bacteria are there? Not 24, not 240, but over 16 MILLION! This explosive growth is the power of exponential functions!
exponential.where: where a = initial value, b = base (b > 0, b ≠ 1), and x = exponent

comparison.title: Exponential vs Linear Growth
comparison.intro: The difference between exponential and linear growth is dramatic—exponential functions grow MUCH faster!

comparison.title: Linear vs Exponential Growth
comparison.caption: Watch how exponential growth explodes!
comparison.note: Notice: By x = 5, exponential is already 3× larger than linear!

example2.title: Example 2: Compound Interest
example2.problem: You invest $1000 at 5% annual interest compounded yearly. How much after 5 years?

example3.title: Example 3: Population Growth
example3.problem: A bacteria population doubles every hour. Starting with 100, how many after 4 hours?

mistake1.title: Confusing Exponentiation with Multiplication
mistake1.explanation: Exponents mean repeated multiplication, NOT multiplying the base by the exponent. 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3 = 6!
mistake1.tip: Remember: The exponent tells you HOW MANY TIMES to multiply the base by itself.

mistake2.title: Negative Exponent Errors
mistake2.explanation: A negative exponent doesn't make the answer negative—it makes it a fraction! Think: 3⁻² = 1/3² = 1/9 (positive fraction).

mistake3.title: Thinking Exponential and Polynomial Grow the Same
mistake3.wrong: Students think y = x³ and y = 3ˣ grow at similar rates:
mistake3.correct: Exponential functions grow MUCH faster than any polynomial:
mistake3.explanation: At x = 10: x³ = 1,000 but 3ˣ = 59,049! Exponential growth accelerates while polynomial growth stays steady. This is why compound interest and viral spread are so powerful!

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
realWorld.intro: Exponential functions model some of the most important phenomena in our world—from pandemics to investments!

app1.title: 🦠 Population Growth & Epidemics
app1.description: Populations grow exponentially when resources are unlimited.
app1.example: COVID-19 spread exponentially initially. If each person infects 2 others, growth follows N(t) = N₀ · 2ᵗ

app2.title: 💵 Compound Interest & Savings
app2.description: Your money grows exponentially when interest compounds.
app2.example: Invest $1000 at 7% annually: A = 1000(1.07)ᵗ. After 30 years: $7,612! The power of exponential growth.

app3.title: ☢️ Radioactive Decay
app3.description: Radioactive materials decay exponentially over time.
app3.example: Carbon-14 used in dating fossils follows N(t) = N₀(0.5)^(t/5730), where half decays every 5,730 years

exercise2.question: If f(x) = 2ˣ, what is f(4)? Enter the number.

exercise3.question: Which function represents exponential growth?
exercise3.explanation: f(x) = 2ˣ is exponential (variable in exponent). The others are polynomial or linear.

exercise4.question: A population doubles every year. Starting with 100, how many after 4 years? Enter the number.

exercise5.question: Which represents exponential decay?
exercise5.explanation: f(x) = (1/3)ˣ has base 1/3 which is between 0 and 1, causing exponential decay.

exercise6.question: A substance decays exponentially: N(t) = 81 · (1/3)ᵗ. After how many time periods will only 3 units remain? Enter the number.

notes.title: Tips & Strategies
notes.tip1: 📝 In exponential functions y = abˣ, the base b determines growth (b > 1) or decay (0 < b < 1).
notes.tip2: 🎯 Exponential functions NEVER touch the x-axis—they approach it but never reach zero!
notes.tip3: 💡 When comparing growth rates, exponential ALWAYS beats polynomial eventually, no matter how large the polynomial degree!
notes.warning1: ⚠️ Don't confuse 2ˣ with x²! In 2ˣ the variable is the exponent; in x² the variable is the base.

conclusion.title: You've Unlocked Exponential Power! 🚀
conclusion.summary: Exponential functions describe rapid change in the natural world, from bacterial growth to radioactive decay. Understanding exponential growth is crucial in today's world—from understanding pandemics to managing investments!
conclusion.takeaway1: Exponential functions have the form f(x) = a · bˣ where b > 0, b ≠ 1
conclusion.takeaway2: Base b > 1 creates growth; 0 < b < 1 creates decay
conclusion.takeaway3: Exponential growth eventually surpasses any polynomial growth
conclusion.takeaway4: Real-world applications include compound interest, population, and radioactive decay
